name: Show Marquee
author: Chuck Hergenroeder
description: Turns an LED matrix into a sign for your light show: your show's name and logo, a Christmas countdown, your show times, the weather, your social media handles, a QR code for your show's audio app (PulseMesh or Tune2) and your own messages, taking turns. Weather is off until you turn it on, then comes from your own Tempest station or Open-Meteo (api.open-meteo.com, which receives this player's location rounded to about 1 km).

privacy.summary: Draws your show's sign pages on a matrix here. With Weather on, it gets weather from Open-Meteo (sending your location, rounded) or hears your Tempest station on your network.

sends.to: http://the FPP player you set as FPP Host (this device by default)
sends.what: requests for the list of overlay models and to turn the chosen model on and off
sends.why: to draw your sign's pages on a matrix attached to that player

sends.what: this player's latitude and longitude, rounded to about 1 km, every 15 minutes
sends.why: for the weather page: temperature, wind and day or night; only with Open-Meteo chosen

collects.what: a weather location you type in instead of FPP's own (latitude and longitude)
your show's logo, if you upload one for the Show page

systemChanges.what: runs a background program whenever FPP is running, which draws your sign's pages
its background program listens on 127.0.0.1:32330, reachable only from this device; FPP's web server passes requests to it
with Weather on, listens for UDP broadcasts on port 50222 (shared with other listeners) to read a Tempest station; sends nothing

privacy.other: Its API is served through FPP's web server, so anyone who can open this player's FPP pages can change its settings and turn its output on or off, the same as FPP itself. Its FPP commands (countdown on/off, set target) do the same from anything that can run FPP commands, including the scheduler, MQTT and other FPP players. It switches the overlay model you choose on and off and writes pixels into that model's overlay buffer. It writes an activity log (logs/plugin-fpp-showmarquee.log). Uninstalling removes its settings (config/plugin.fpp-showmarquee.json) and what it keeps in plugindata/fpp-showmarquee/ (a weather location you type in, the Show page's logo); a Reinstall keeps them on FPP 10.4 and later. The show prep page's QR code holds a link to the app's download page (pulsemesh.io or tune2.app, or a link you type in): viewers' phones open it, the plugin itself never contacts those sites.
